title: Detectors: CCDs and Photomultipliers
welcome_lead: Turn photons into pixels — the heart of every modern instrument.
meta_desc: A-Level Astronomy: CCDs, quantum efficiency and photomultipliers.
final_note: Detector choice shapes what an observation can achieve.

concepts.def: Charge-Coupled Device — silicon array converting photons to charge.
Vacuum tube amplifying single photons into measurable pulses.
Picture element — one cell of a detector array.
Thermal signal generated even without light.
Noise added when reading each pixel out.

walkthroughs.body_html: A CCD is a grid of silicon pixels. Photons release electrons that accumulate in each pixel; the charge is shifted out for digitisation. CCDs reach quantum efficiency above 90% in the optical.

PMTs turn a single photon striking a photocathode into a cascade of millions of electrons. They are fast and sensitive but cover only one pixel — useful for timing, photometry and cosmic ray detection.
Real detectors fight read noise, dark current and photon shot noise. Cooling reduces dark current; longer exposures help shot noise (S/N grows as sqrt(t)).
